The information about other applicants' preferences is useful, but doesn't change my own value assessment.

My values are: w = $53, x = $79, y = $73, z = $63. Therefore, my most preferred school is x ($79), followed by y ($73), then z ($63), and finally w ($53).

The fact that y is popular doesn't dissuade me from ranking it second – I might still get it! And even if I don't, being rejected by y doesn't affect my chances at z or w. Similarly, my high priority at w and y doesn't change the fundamental value I place on each school. I should simply rank them in order of my value.
